one_line: A woman (introduced only by her own spoken claim as a pediatric dietitian) talks to camera, cut out over a heavy-metals web page, a soil diagram and the brand's test table, and ends by recommending Cerebelly baby food because it tests every batch.

hook.visual: Speaker cut out in the bottom right over a full-screen web page headed 'Heavy Metals and Juice'; a solid blue label sits across the page heading. Burned-in captions start at about 1.5 s.
hook.on_screen_text: Why are there heavy metals in baby food? (blue label over the page heading 'Heavy Metals ... and Juice')
hook.first_spoken_line: If you feel like you're getting mixed messages about heavy metals in baby food, here are the facts minus the fear-mongering and exactly what to do about it. (spoken, English)
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: It names a specific parent fear in the label and the first sentence, then promises plain facts and 'exactly what to do about it' (inferred open loop). The blue question label is readable with sound off, and the page behind her looks like a real news or health source (inferred).

beats.observed: Speaker bottom right over a screenshot-style web page 'Heavy Metals and Juice' with small body text and plus-sign accordion items; blue question label over the title; white burned-in captions with dark outline appear from about 1.5 s (none in the 0.0 frame).

beats.observed: Background switches to an infographic: top half shows a smokestack, a worker with a backpack sprayer, plants in soil with grey spheres carrying element symbols, arrows labelled 'Heavy Metals Deposition' (down) and 'Heavy Metals Uptake' (up); bottom half shows labelled root-vegetable drawings (Daikon, Turnip, Beet, Parsnip legible, others cut off by the speaker). A pointing hand enters near the upper right at about 12.0 s. Captions follow the speech.

payoff: The 'why are metals in food' answer (soil, root vegetables) lands at 7.2 to 16.7 s; the 'what to do about it' answer (pick a brand that tests, here Cerebelly) lands at 26.5 to 39.4 s, so the promised action is held to the last third.
cta: No explicit ask (no link, buy or follow prompt observed). The implied ask is to choose a baby food brand that tests batches, named as Cerebelly in the last 13 s.
share_or_comment_trigger: Reassurance for anxious parents is something one might send to a partner or friend, but the numbers say it rarely happened: 22 shares and 9 comments on 106,900 views (about 0.02 percent share rate, 0.008 percent comment rate).
why_it_worked: Reach, not engagement, drove it: 106,900 views is 194.7x the account median of 549, while likes (565), comments (9) and shares (22) stay tiny for that audience.
Topic and hook hit a live parent fear (heavy metals in baby food) with a plain-language promise in the first 7 s, and the question label works muted.
A new visual every 6 to 13 s (page, soil diagram, puree bowls, brand test table, product shot) keeps a 39 s explainer moving, and the brand pitch is held until the last third after the useful fact.
paid_signal: unclear: like_rate 0.53 percent is above the 0.3 percent paid flag, but a 549-view median spiking to 106,900 with 9 comments, plus a scripted brand recommendation, is consistent with a boosted or partnership post; this is inference only.

solo_route.how: 1) Pick one real parent worry from comments or DMs and write a 3-bullet answer with a barter expert. 2) The expert films a vertical selfie of about 30 s on a phone. 3) In CapCut, use background removal to cut her out, place her bottom right over Canva slides (a simple explainer graphic, then a proof screenshot), and add a solid label with the question over the first 7 s. 4) Add auto-captions in Hebrew, correct the brand name by hand, and put the brand mention only in the last third.
solo_route.needs: A barter expert willing to appear on camera (the on-camera credential is the point), a written source for every factual claim, and rights to any screenshots or third-party graphics used. Any safety or certification proof must be real and supplied by LumeBook's printer or supplier.

lumebook_version.hook_he: הילד מבקש את אותו ספר בפעם ה-20? מומחית שפה מסבירה, בלי הגזמות
lumebook_version.concept: A barter child-language specialist answers one worry parents actually have (a child demanding the same book again and again) in a 30 s talking head, cut out over simple Canva visuals. The soft LumeBook mention comes only in the last 5 s, as the place where repeat reading feels special.

evidence_notes: Transcript is full speech and matches the burned-in captions closely, so spoken content is medium to high reliability. Whisper wrote 'Cerebelli' while the burned-in captions say 'Cerave' (an auto-caption error, observed). The speaker is not named anywhere on screen; 'pediatric dietitian' is her own spoken claim and the video does not prove it. 'Test every batch' and 'strictest standards' are spoken brand claims, not shown to be verified. The soil diagram labels Daikon, Turnip, Beet and Parsnip, while carrots and sweet potatoes are only spoken. Small table values were read at 36.0 s and are only partly legible elsewhere. creator_collab is inferred from third-person brand-recommendation wording on a brand account, not stated. Audio and tone not assessed.
